Reference

Requirements, lifecycle and operations

This page lists every normative statement of the lifecycle and operations lane, one row each, with its test. The ids have the form LIF-nnn. Contract version: ilium:plugin@0.1.0.

How to read the rows

  • MUST and MUST NOT mark a rule a host has to meet. SHOULD marks a rule to follow unless there is a stated reason. MAY marks a choice.
  • An id is never reused. A removed rule keeps its number and is marked removed.
  • Each row links to the page that explains the rule. The page is the source. This table is built from it.
  • The platform is not implemented. A test is a description of how to check, written for the fake host and for a real host.

Plugin states and transitions

Id Requirement Test Page
LIF-001 The host MUST give every installed plugin exactly one package state at any time. list a plugin through every transition below and assert one state in ilium plugin list --json. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-002 A stop by failure belongs to one side, not to the package. It is the instance state stopped-by-failure of that side, and the package state stays installed-enabled. A stop of the client side MUST NOT stop the server side. trap the client side three times and assert the server side stays active. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-003 A package with state refused-at-load MUST NOT be instantiated, and the refusal code MUST be shown in disabled-reason. install a package whose api window the host does not support and read the list output. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-004 disabled-by-policy and safe mode MUST NOT be written to installed.json. start in safe mode, stop, start normally and assert the plugin is installed-enabled again. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-005 An instance MUST be in exactly one instance state, and only the transitions in the tables below MAY occur. a state-machine fuzz test drives random triggers and asserts every observed transition is in the table. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-006 The host MUST NOT call handler, views, renderer or provider exports on an instance that is not active. send an event to an instance in activating and assert it is queued, and an event to stopped is dropped. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-007 Enabling a plugin that is refused-at-load or disabled-by-policy MUST return not-permitted with the refusal code in the message, and MUST NOT change any state. call set-enabled(id, true) on a policy-blocked plugin. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-008 A failure that moves the server side to stopped-by-failure MUST be written to failure_stopped in installed.json, so it survives a server restart. A client or scene side is not stored. cause three failures, restart the server and read the list output. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-009 Enabling, resetting failures or installing an update MUST clear the failure window of the sides it affects. two failures, then enable, then one failure restarts after the first-failure delay. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-010 A candidate whose first activate fails MUST roll back to the previous version, as P10 says, and MUST NOT leave the plugin in update-staged. A failure after a successful first activation MUST NOT roll back. stage a version whose activate always errors and assert the old version is active. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-011 The host MUST apply row I2 when the session memory pool cannot admit the instance, and MUST NOT count that refusal as a failure. fill the pool with other plugins, trigger activation and assert the failure window of the refused plugin is empty. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-012 A trap, an error from activate or a deadline breach in activating or active MUST follow rows I4 or I5 and MUST drop the instance without calling deactivate. trap in on-events and assert no deactivate call is logged. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-013 The host MUST apply row I14 when a plugin is disabled, updated or uninstalled while a restart is scheduled. schedule a restart, disable the plugin and assert the timer never fires. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-014 Rows I9 to I13 MUST send exactly one deactivate call per live instance, with the reason in the table. for each row, count deactivate calls and read the reason. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-015 A client or scene instance MUST receive deactivate(shutdown) when its client disconnects cleanly, and MUST receive no other reason. After a crash or a kill of the client process no call is possible: the server uses the last restore bytes it stored. kill the client process and read the server log for the stored restore bytes. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-016 The host MUST emit plugin-state-changed once per state change, in the order the changes happened, to every subscriber with plugins.manage. record events through a full disable, enable and failure sequence. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-017 plugins.list MUST return one record per installed plugin with every field of the plugin-info table, in table order. install two plugins, disable one and compare the records with the table. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-018 enabled MUST equal the rule above in every state. parametrised over the eight package states. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-019 set-enabled(id, true) on an enabled plugin and set-enabled(id, false) on a disabled plugin MUST return ok and change nothing, and no event MUST be emitted. call twice and count events. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-020 The host MUST serialise all transitions of one plugin id. Transitions of different plugin ids MAY run in parallel. issue disable and uninstall at the same time and assert one runs after the other. Reference, plugin lifecycle states

Failure counting, restart and activation

Id Requirement Test Page
LIF-025 The host MUST keep one failure window for each combination of plugin id, side and scope. The scope is the session server for the server side, and one attached client connection for the client and scene sides. attach two clients, trap the plugin twice on client A and once on client B, and assert that failures-in-window is 2 and 1. Lifecycle
LIF-026 Two clients MUST NOT share a window. Disabling the plugin by failure on client A MUST NOT stop it on client B or on the server. as above, with a third trap on client A. Lifecycle
LIF-027 A window MUST be a sliding window of 10 minutes on a monotonic clock. A failure counts while its age is less than 600 s. with the FakeHost advance_clock, trap at 0 s, advance 599 s and assert the failure counts, advance 2 s more and assert it does not. Lifecycle
LIF-028 The first counted failure in a window MUST schedule a restart after 1 s. trap once and read restart-at. Lifecycle
LIF-029 The second counted failure in a window MUST schedule a restart after 5 s. trap twice within 10 minutes. Lifecycle
LIF-030 The third counted failure in a window MUST stop that side with the instance state stopped-by-failure and MUST NOT schedule a restart. The package state stays installed-enabled. trap three times within 10 minutes and assert no activation follows. Lifecycle
LIF-031 The host MUST NOT use any other restart delay. There is no step after the second, because the third failure stops the side. after a stop, advance the clock one hour and assert the side is still stopped. Lifecycle
LIF-032 The host MUST NOT add random jitter. The delay timer starts when the instance is dropped. The next activation MUST NOT begin earlier than the delay, and SHOULD begin within 250 ms after it. assert the begin time is in the range delay to delay plus 250 ms. Lifecycle
LIF-033 The host MUST count each kind in the table as the table says. a parametrised test, one case per row, reading failures-in-window. Lifecycle
LIF-034 A refusal caused by host capacity MUST NOT count against the plugin. The instance stays inactive with the reason host-capacity. The host MUST retry the activation when pool memory is released, and in any case 1 s, 5 s and 30 s after the refusal, then every 60 s without end while the plugin is enabled. fill the pool, trigger activation, assert failures-in-window is 0, free memory and assert the activation runs. Lifecycle
LIF-035 A failed job MUST NOT count. trap inside a job and assert failures-in-window is unchanged. Lifecycle
LIF-036 Enabling the plugin, the command ilium plugin reset-failures <id>, the Enable action of the recovery page and installing an update MUST clear the failure window of the affected sides. two traps, then each action, then one trap restarts after 1 s. Lifecycle
LIF-037 The instance state stopped-by-failure of the server side MUST be written to failure_stopped in installed.json and MUST survive a server restart. The failure window itself MUST NOT; it starts empty. The state of a client or scene side MUST be dropped when its client detaches. stop the server after a stop-by-failure and assert the state after the restart; detach and reattach a client and assert the client side runs again. Lifecycle
LIF-038 When a server stop begins, the host MUST cancel all pending restart timers and MUST NOT schedule a new one. A failure during shutdown is logged and not counted. schedule a restart, begin a stop and assert no activation. Lifecycle
LIF-039 When the user disables the plugin while a restart is pending, the host MUST cancel the timer and move the side to installed-disabled-by-user. schedule, disable, advance the clock past the delay and assert no activation. Lifecycle
LIF-040 When an update arrives while a restart is pending, the host MUST cancel the timer, clear the window and activate the new version by its normal triggers. schedule, update, assert the new version activates. Lifecycle
LIF-041 A revocation or grant while a restart is pending MUST keep the timer. The new instance MUST receive the current granted list. schedule, revoke a grant, assert the restarted instance sees the shorter list. Lifecycle
LIF-042 An essential core plugin (see Core plugins) MUST never be stopped by failure. Its third and later failures in a window MUST restart after 5 s and MUST raise the essential-failure banner. trap ilium.core.tree three times and assert it restarts and the banner shows. Lifecycle
LIF-043 The enum deactivation-reason MUST have the six values above, and the host MUST send crash-restart never. enumerate the reasons seen across a full lifecycle test. Lifecycle
LIF-044 A production update MUST send upgrade to every live instance of the old version before the swap. update an active plugin and read the deactivation reason. Lifecycle
LIF-045 The host MUST compute the start order of startup plugins with Kahn's algorithm over the edges of the non-optional requires.plugins entries and of the requires.services entries to their providers. A provider's activate MUST return before any consumer that requires it begins activate. three plugins, A requires B requires C, record the order of activate.begin. Lifecycle
LIF-046 At each step of that algorithm the host MUST take the ready node with the smallest key: the tier number (T1 first), then the plugin id in ascending byte order. install T1 b, T2 a and T1 a with no dependencies and assert the order T1 a, T1 b, T2 a. Lifecycle
LIF-047 Independent plugins MAY activate in parallel. The host MUST run at most 4 concurrent activations per side, and MUST start them in the order of LIF-046. 12 independent plugins, each blocking in activate, and assert the peak is 4 and that the begin order is the key order. Lifecycle
LIF-048 A cycle in the non-optional requires.services entries MUST be refused at install, at stage 10, with manifest.service-cycle. A cycle in requires.plugins is refused with dependency.cycle. The rules for both are in Versions and dependencies. install two plugins that require each other's services and read the code and the cycle order. Lifecycle
LIF-049 Dependencies are requires.plugins and requires.services. The host version is checked only through requires.host, which is refused with dependency.host-version at stage 10. A key named engines is refused with manifest.unknown-key. install a manifest with requires.host above the running release, and one with an engines key. Lifecycle
LIF-050 On server stop the host MUST call deactivate(shutdown) in the exact reverse of the start order, one at a time, so that a consumer stops before the providers it requires. The order of completion of the starts does not matter. record the order of deactivate calls after a start in which activations finished in a different order. Lifecycle
LIF-051 A consumer MUST stay active when its provider fails, is disabled or is uninstalled. disable the provider and assert the consumer state. Lifecycle
LIF-052 The host MUST return the code in the table for a service call. one case per row. Lifecycle
LIF-053 The host MUST send the event service-availability-changed (interface, available, provider) to every active consumer when the availability of a required interface changes. disable and enable the provider and read the events. Lifecycle
LIF-054 When the user disables a plugin that is a provider for other plugins, the disable dialog MUST list the dependants, and the CLI MUST print a warning line for each dependant. The disable is not blocked. disable a provider and read the dialog text. Lifecycle
LIF-055 The host MUST activate the owner of an extension point before its contributors. After the owner's activate returns, the host MUST activate in the background the lazy contributors of its points, so that a contribution needs no trigger of its own. a lazy contributor to a hook point becomes active after the owner activates. Lifecycle
LIF-056 A hook call MUST NOT wait for a contributor that is not yet active. The host skips it, treats it as pass and logs extension.contributor-not-ready. call a hook while the contributor is activating. Lifecycle
LIF-057 If the server and a client run different versions of one plugin, each side MUST keep running the version it has until it receives the change notice for the update. The host MUST NOT block messages between the sides. update a plugin while a client is attached and assert both sides finish on the new version. Lifecycle
LIF-058 A client whose API version differs from the server's MUST be refused at the handshake with the message api-version mismatch naming both versions. connect a client with a different API version. Lifecycle
LIF-059 The client SHOULD render its first frame when the essential client plugins are active, or after 1,000 ms, whichever comes first. Plugins that are not active by then continue to activate in the background, and the first frame shows a starting plugins mark. delay a non-essential plugin by 3 s and assert the first frame appears within 1,100 ms. Lifecycle

Install, update, rollback and uninstall

Id Requirement Test Page
LIF-065 The host MUST write installed.json atomically: write a temporary file in the same directory, fsync it, rename it over the old file, then fsync the directory. kill the writer at each step (fault injection) and assert that a reader sees the old or the new file, never a partial one. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-066 The host MUST hold installed.lock while it changes the store or the registry. A second writer MUST wait up to 30 s, then fail with install.locked and exit code 4. hold the lock and start an install. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-067 The host MUST refuse a registry whose format is higher than it knows, with install.registry-format, and MUST NOT rewrite it. set format to 99. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-068 The host MUST NOT instantiate or run any code of the package before step 7 has finished. install a package whose start function writes a file and decline the review; assert the file is absent. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-069 A failure at any step MUST leave the registry byte for byte unchanged and MUST delete the staging directory and any new store entry. inject a failure at each step and compare the registry hash. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-070 An install MUST NOT require network access. run the install in a network namespace with no interfaces. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-071 Steps 2 to 6 MUST run in the order of the table, so that the cheapest checks refuse first and no prompt appears for a package that would be refused later. a package with a bad signature and a bad manifest reports signature.invalid. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-072 Installing the same id and version again MUST succeed without change when the manifest hash is equal, and MUST fail with install.same-version-different-content when it differs. install a package twice, then a modified copy with the same version. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-073 The first server to apply an update MUST decide it. After step 6, a failure on another server MUST follow the normal failure rule and MUST NOT roll back. update with two servers running, fail the second server's activation and assert the version stays. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-074 An update MUST be atomic: after any interruption, either the old or the new version is active, never neither. kill the installer or the server at each step and assert that a plugin version is active after restart. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-075 A failed activation of the candidate MUST roll back to the previous version and its data snapshot automatically. install a candidate whose activate returns an error. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-076 The host MUST keep exactly one previous version in store/ and delete older ones after a committed update. update three times and list store/<id>/. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-077 A blocked candidate MUST NOT be tried again unless the user installs it again explicitly. roll back, restart the server and assert that no activation of the candidate occurs. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-078 An update MUST NOT send grants to the new version beyond those the user accepted. A new version that asks for more is update-staged until the review is answered. update with an extra grant and decline. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-079 Activating a version whose data_version is lower than the stamp of any bucket in scope MUST be refused with migration.data-newer (stage I, exit 1), unless --restore-backup or --discard-data is given. This applies to downgrade and rollback. --restore-backup restores the data snapshot taken before the update and loses what was written since. --discard-data deletes the plugin's buckets and data directory. update to a version that migrates data, write data, roll back without a flag and assert migration.data-newer; repeat with each flag Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-080 --restore-backup MUST fail with rollback.no-backup when the snapshot is gone. delete the backup and roll back with the flag. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-081 Rollback MUST send deactivate(upgrade) to the running instances and activate the previous version with the same rules as an update. read the reasons in the log. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-082 Without a TTY, an uninstall with neither --purge nor --keep-data MUST keep the data directory and the buckets. run it with standard input closed. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-083 The host MUST delete grants, first-use answers, durable timers, failure counters and persistent decorations on every uninstall. A reinstall MUST ask for grants again. install, grant, uninstall, install and assert the review dialog appears. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-084 Node metadata and session data of an uninstalled plugin MUST stay inert: the host never passes them to another plugin, and keeps them in the snapshot. A reinstall of the same id MAY read them again. With --purge the host MUST delete them in the live session and add a tombstone, so that other projects delete theirs when they next open. purge, reopen another project and assert the keys are gone. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-085 Uninstall MUST first set uninstall-pending, then stop all instances, then delete files. After a crash, the next start MUST finish it. kill the host after the state is written. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-086 Uninstall MUST NOT delete data of other plugins, and MUST NOT remove a publisher key. compare the other plugins' directories before and after. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-087 Every command MUST print only JSON lines on standard output when output is not a terminal, MUST use the exit codes above and MUST give each error line a code from this page. run each command in a pipe and parse every line. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-088 enable and disable MUST be idempotent: they exit 0 and print a result line with changed: false when nothing changes. disable twice. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-089 A server MUST watch installed.json and apply a change within 2 s of the write. If the watch is not available, it MUST poll every 5 s. The installing CLI MUST also send a plugins-changed message to every server it can find in the runtime directory; a server it cannot reach is reported as a warning line with install.notify-failed and picks the change up at its watch or at its next start. install with two servers, assert both log registry.changed within 2 s. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-090 A server that is not running MUST use the registry as it finds it at start. install, then start a server and assert the new version is active. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-091 A change MUST be applied to a server under the per-plugin serialisation of lifecycle states. install an update during a disable. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-092 At start, and at the start of every ilium plugin command that takes the lock, the host MUST delete staging directories whose creating process is gone or that are older than 1 hour. create an orphan staging directory and start a server. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-093 A store entry with no registry entry and older than 1 hour MUST be deleted at start. A registry entry whose store entry is missing or fails its hash check MUST put the plugin in refused-at-load with package.corrupt. ilium plugin reinstall <id> MUST repair it from the cached package or fail with package.cache-missing. truncate a file in the store. Reference, install, update and uninstall
LIF-094 After a power loss the host MUST find either the old or the new registry, because of LIF-065, and MUST finish or undo an update in trial by the rules above at the next activation. kill the machine at step 11 (simulated) and restart. Reference, install, update and uninstall

Data migration and storage

Id Requirement Test Page
LIF-100 The manifest key data_version MUST be an unsigned 32-bit integer. When absent it MUST be 1. A value of 0 or a non-integer MUST be refused with manifest.data-version. install manifests with 0, 1, "2" and 4294967295. Guide, data migration
LIF-101 The host MUST store the data version of each bucket and of the data directory in a place the plugin cannot read or write, and MUST stamp it only after a successful migration or on first creation. read the stamp through the CLI ilium plugin info <id> --json after a migration. Guide, data migration
LIF-102 The host MUST NOT migrate data it did not stamp itself. A bucket with no stamp (created before the plugin ever stored data) MUST be stamped with the current data_version at first write. first put on a new plugin. Guide, data migration
LIF-103 The host MUST drop restore bytes when the data_version of the running version differs from that of the version that produced them, and MUST log restore.dropped-data-version. change data_version between two builds and read restored. Guide, data migration
LIF-104 For each bucket, the host MUST call migrate(from, to) at most once per update, the first time a host instance activates with that bucket in scope and the bucket stamp is lower than data_version, with from less than to. The global bucket and the data directory migrate at the first activation after the swap. A project or session bucket migrates when its session first activates the plugin. update from 1 to 3, open two sessions, and assert one call (1, 3) for the global bucket and one for each session bucket Guide, data migration
LIF-105 A call that returns an error, traps or misses the deadline MUST be a migration failure (LIF-108). It MUST NOT count toward the failure window of the plugin. return an error from migrate and read failures-in-window. Guide, data migration
LIF-106 migrate MUST be idempotent. The host MAY call it again with the same arguments after an interrupted run (LIF-110). run the call twice on a fixture and compare the data. Guide, data migration
LIF-107 The host MUST copy the global, project and session buckets in use and the data directory to backups/<id>/<version>-<utc timestamp>/ before it calls migrate. The timestamp has the form YYYYMMDDTHHmmssZ. The host MUST refuse with install.no-space, before touching any data, when free space is less than twice the data size plus 100 MiB. The backup size is capped by the key migration_backup_mib in the [plugins] table of config.toml (integer 0 to 1048576, default 2048; 0 disables backups). Data above the cap is refused with migration.backup-too-large (stage I, exit 1) unless --no-backup is given, and then a failed migration cannot be undone. A copy-on-write copy MAY replace the full copy. fill the disk and update; set the cap to 1 and update with 2 MiB of data, with and without --no-backup Guide, data migration
LIF-108 On a migration failure the host MUST restore the backup, keep the previous version active, log migration.failed with the plugin's error code and message, and mark the update rolled back. fail migrate after it wrote half the keys, then compare the buckets with the backup. Guide, data migration
LIF-109 After an update that succeeded and was activated, the host MUST keep only the newest backup of that plugin and delete older ones in backups/<id>/. update twice and list the backups Guide, data migration
LIF-110 At the next start the host MUST restore the backup, increment update.attempts in installed.json and run the update again from the beginning. The host MUST write update.state: "migrating" and the attempt count with fsync before it calls migrate. When attempts reaches 2 it MUST roll back with migration.interrupted and mark the candidate skip. kill the process in the middle of migrate twice and assert the rollback and skip Guide, data migration
LIF-111 The host MUST refuse to activate a version whose data_version is lower than the stamp of any bucket in scope, with migration.data-newer. The user may run the command with --restore-backup (the host restores the backup taken before the update) or --discard-data (the host deletes the plugin's buckets and data directory). roll back after a migration, with and without each flag. This is the same rule as LIF-079. Guide, data migration
LIF-112 A migration that touches the global bucket or the data directory MUST hold the cross-process lock plugins/locks/<id>.migrate.lock. The other servers MUST first deactivate their old instances with upgrade, then wait for the lock for at most the migrate deadline plus 5 s, and then skip the migration when they find the stamp already new. update with two servers, count calls to migrate. Guide, data migration
LIF-113 While the stamp of the global bucket is higher than the data version of a running instance, a put, write-batch or remove from that instance MUST return conflict with the message stale-data-version. leave one server on the old version and write to the global bucket. Guide, data migration
LIF-114 A project bucket and a session bucket MUST be migrated by the session that opens them, each with its own backup. open two projects after an update. Guide, data migration
LIF-115 put and write-batch MUST return only after the data is committed to stable storage with a flush, so that a power loss after the return does not lose it. kill the process after a put returns and read it back. Guide, data migration
LIF-116 If a plugin must change several files of its data directory, it SHOULD write a new set of files first and write a version marker file last, so that a crash leaves either the old set or the complete new set. The host does not give transactions for files. kill the host between the two writes and assert the plugin reads the old set. Guide, data migration
LIF-117 write-batch MUST apply all its entries or none of them. A batch holds at most 256 entries and at most 4 MiB of key and value bytes together; more is invalid-argument. A refused batch keeps every previous value. write a batch whose last entry breaks the quota and read all keys. storage
LIF-118 put, remove and write-batch MUST return only after the change is flushed to stable storage, so that a crash or power loss after the return cannot lose it. A crash before the return leaves the previous value. kill the process in the middle of a batch and read back. storage
LIF-119 A write that fails because the disk is full MUST return io with the message no-space, never quota-exceeded, which is only for the plugin's own quota. fill the disk and put. See offline and low disk. storage
LIF-120 Several session servers can write the same global or project bucket. The host MUST serialise writers with a lock per bucket, so that each put and each batch is atomic across processes, and the last writer of a key wins. There is no compare-and-set; use a version key and write-batch if you need one. two servers write the same key and read it back. storage
LIF-121 The bucket also carries a data version stamp that the plugin cannot see. A write from an instance older than the stamp MUST return conflict with the message stale-data-version. See data migration. see LIF-113. storage

Health and watchdog

Id Requirement Test Page
LIF-122 The host MUST compute health from the first matching row of the first table, and MUST report it in plugin-info, in ilium plugin status and on the Plugins screen. drive a plugin into each state and read the value. Reference, health and watchdog
LIF-123 The host MUST use the thresholds and time spans in the second table. with advance_clock, produce 4 and then 5 near-misses and assert the change, and wait 5 minutes and assert the return to healthy. Reference, health and watchdog
LIF-124 A plugin that is stopped, disabled or dormant MUST NOT be reported degraded. disable a degraded plugin. Reference, health and watchdog
LIF-125 The host MUST interrupt a call that runs longer than its deadline D at a time t with D <= t <= D + 20 ms of wall time measured from the start of the call, on a host that is not overloaded. a plugin that loops forever; assert the trap time is in [D, D + 20] ms, and that a call that returns at D - 1 ms never traps. Reference, health and watchdog
LIF-126 The host MUST NOT interrupt a call before its deadline. a call that takes 0.9 times D completes. Reference, health and watchdog
LIF-127 The host MUST NOT use fuel to enforce deadlines. build the engine configuration and assert that fuel is off. Reference, health and watchdog
LIF-128 The tick MUST be 10 ms in every process and the instance deadline MUST be ceil(D / 10) + 1 ticks after the call starts. read the engine configuration. Reference, health and watchdog
LIF-129 Wall time spent inside a synchronous host call MUST count toward the deadline of the export that made it. Time waiting for an asynchronous request MUST NOT. a handler that calls a slow synchronous host function (fixture clock) and a handler that waits for a request. Reference, health and watchdog
LIF-130 The host MUST complete all pending requests of a dropped or deactivated instance as cancelled, and MUST NOT call into the instance for them. drop an instance with three pending requests and count outcomes. Reference, health and watchdog
LIF-131 A request that has no reply within its timeout MUST complete as timed-out. a service that never answers. Reference, health and watchdog
LIF-132 A hung helper MUST be killed after 3 missed heartbeats or 500 ms past a deadline, whichever is first. a helper that stops answering. Reference, health and watchdog
LIF-133 After a helper dies, the host MUST count one failure for the plugin that was running and none for the others, and MUST restart the others at once in a new helper. crash a helper hosting three plugins and read the three windows. Reference, health and watchdog
LIF-134 The host MUST restart a helper after a crash at most 5 times in 10 minutes. After that, the T2 and T3 plugins of the session MUST move to stopped-by-failure on the server side with the reason helper.unstable. kill the helper six times. Reference, health and watchdog
LIF-135 The host MUST keep the metrics above for each plugin and side, and MUST discard buckets older than 24 hours. read the metrics after 25 simulated hours. Reference, health and watchdog
LIF-136 A server restart MUST reset the metrics. restart and read. Reference, health and watchdog
LIF-137 ilium plugin status MUST print the health and the metrics of every installed plugin, as JSON lines when output is not a terminal. run it in a pipe and parse. Reference, health and watchdog
LIF-138 The diagnostics report MUST contain a Plugins section with the health of every plugin that is not healthy. degrade a plugin and generate the report. Reference, health and watchdog

Resource accounting

Id Requirement Test Page
LIF-139 The host MUST charge thread CPU time of each call to the ilium-execution group of the plugin side, and MUST refuse a submission with quota-exceeded and a retry-after-ms when the bucket is empty. a plugin that submits in a loop; assert the refusal, the retry value, and that the plugin is not restarted. Reference, resource accounting
LIF-140 A refusal for quota MUST NOT count as a failure. read the failure window after 100 refusals. Reference, resource accounting
LIF-141 An instance whose reservation does not fit MUST stay inactive with the reason host-capacity, MUST NOT be counted as a failure, and MUST start when memory is freed. fill the pool with a small session_memory_mib, activate one more plugin, then deactivate another. Reference, resource accounting
LIF-142 A core T1 plugin MUST be admitted before any third-party plugin at server start. set a pool that fits exactly the core plugins plus one more, and start with a third-party plugin that activates on startup. Reference, resource accounting
LIF-143 The effective limit MUST be min(ceiling, first set of [plugins."<id>".limits] value, [plugins.limits] value, manifest value, default); 0 or a missing value means not set, so the next source applies. The user can raise a value up to the ceiling and can lower it. Session keys have no manifest value and the user may only lower them. the three cases of the example. Reference, resource accounting
LIF-144 A per-plugin user value MUST win over a user value for all plugins. set both and read the effective value. Reference, resource accounting
LIF-145 The helper cgroup memory.max MUST equal the sum of the hosted instances' memory_mib plus 32 MiB, the same amount charged to session_memory_mib by HST-164. read the cgroup file for a helper with two instances. Reference, resource accounting
LIF-146 ilium plugin stats MUST print use, effective limit and source for memory, the execution bucket, storage and disk. parse the lines for a fixture plugin. Reference, resource accounting

Persistence and restart

Id Requirement Test Page
LIF-150 The host MUST keep and lose state as the matrix says. one test per column that sets a marker in every row and reads it after the event. Reference, persistence and restart
LIF-151 Pending requests MUST complete as cancelled at every event in the first four columns and MUST NOT be replayed. a pending request across each event. Reference, persistence and restart
LIF-152 Restore bytes over 1 MiB MUST be dropped, and activation.restored MUST be absent. return 1 MiB plus 1 byte. Reference, persistence and restart
LIF-153 Client restore bytes MUST be stored per plugin id, last writer wins, and MUST be passed to the next client activation of that plugin. detach two clients with different bytes and attach a third. Reference, persistence and restart
LIF-154 A failed snapshot write MUST NOT stop the server. The host MUST log snapshot.write-failed, keep the previous snapshot file, and retry at the next snapshot. make the snapshot folder read-only. Reference, persistence and restart
LIF-155 Node metadata MUST survive a plugin restart, an update, a server restart and an uninstall, and MUST be removed with its node. set metadata, run each event, and read it. Reference, persistence and restart
LIF-156 The plugin host MUST start after restore_snapshot and MUST stop before drain_session_work. log the order in a fake kernel. Reference, persistence and restart
LIF-157 A crash of the server (no shutdown) MUST lose only the memory state and the server restore bytes. Storage, settings, data and metadata MUST be as of the last durable write or snapshot. kill the fake server between two writes. Reference, persistence and restart

Scope and sessions

Id Requirement Test Page
LIF-160 The host MUST accept installs only into the user scope in 0.1.0, and MUST refuse --scope project for install with install.scope-unsupported. run the command. Reference, plugin scope and sessions
LIF-161 The effective enabled value MUST follow the order session, project, global. set the three levels in all eight combinations. Reference, plugin scope and sessions
LIF-162 plugins.toml MUST be read as a request only. It MUST NOT install, grant or raise a tier. list a package that is not installed. Reference, plugin scope and sessions
LIF-163 A global enable, disable or uninstall MUST reach every running session of the user within 2 seconds. two fake sessions and a changed file. Reference, plugin scope and sessions
LIF-164 The CLI MUST print one session-result line per session and exit 0 only when all succeeded. make one session unreachable. Reference, plugin scope and sessions
LIF-165 A failure disable MUST apply to the session where it happened and MUST NOT disable the plugin in other sessions. fail a plugin in session A and call it in B. Reference, plugin scope and sessions
LIF-166 A grant change MUST apply to every session and the "Not now" counter MUST be shared. answer in one session and open another. Reference, plugin scope and sessions

Offline and low disk

Id Requirement Test Page
LIF-170 The host MUST load, activate and run installed plugins with no network. block the network in the fixture and start all fixtures. Reference, offline and low disk
LIF-171 Install of a local file MUST NOT contact the network. install with the network blocked. Reference, offline and low disk
LIF-172 The host MUST check free space before install and update, and MUST leave no partial files when it refuses. a small fake volume. Reference, offline and low disk
LIF-173 A disk-full error MUST NOT count as a plugin failure. fill the disk and write. Reference, offline and low disk
LIF-174 A read-only data folder MUST NOT stop the server or the running plugins. mark the folder read-only. Reference, offline and low disk
LIF-175 A corrupt storage database MUST be moved aside and replaced with an empty one, never deleted. write garbage into the file. Reference, offline and low disk

LIF-181 The environment variable MUST behave like the flag, and the flag MUST win. set both to different values. Safe mode and recovery
LIF-182 Safe mode MUST show an indicator in the footer. capture the footer. Safe mode and recovery
LIF-183 The essential set MUST be exactly the four plugins above in 0.1.0, and MUST load in all-optional mode. list running plugins in that mode. Safe mode and recovery

Development reload and other rules

Id Requirement Test Page
LIF-220 ilium plugin dev MUST attach to the session of --cwd (the current directory by default), or to the session named by --session <name>. When no server runs for it, the command MUST exit with code 2 and the error code dev.no-server, unless --start-server is given. run it with no server. Lifecycle
LIF-221 A development package MUST shadow an installed package with the same id for that session only. When ilium plugin dev ends, the installed version MUST become active again. install version 1, run dev with version 2, end dev and read the version. Lifecycle
LIF-222 A rebuild MUST start 300 ms after the last change in the directory. touch a file twice 100 ms apart and assert one build. Lifecycle
LIF-223 The reload steps MUST run in this order: build, validate the manifest, compare grants, deactivate the server side with upgrade, deactivate each attached client side with upgrade in attach order, swap, activate the server side, then each client side, each with restored. record the log order with two clients. Lifecycle
LIF-224 New grants MUST produce a review prompt in the dev terminal, and grants that are no longer in the manifest MUST be revoked without a prompt. With --grant <name> the named grants are accepted without a prompt. A new high-risk grant that is not accepted MUST NOT be granted, and the reload MUST continue with the smaller set. add a grant to the manifest and assert the prompt. Lifecycle
LIF-225 A change to contributions or activation triggers MUST be re-registered at the swap and MUST be followed by ilium.extensions/changed for the affected points. add an extension contribution and read the event. Lifecycle
LIF-226 In dev mode, failures MUST be counted and shown but MUST NOT stop the plugin. The third and later failures restart after 5 s. A successful reload MUST clear the window. trap three times and assert the plugin restarts. Lifecycle
LIF-227 A failed build or a manifest error MUST keep the running instance and print one build-error line. No deactivate MUST be sent. introduce a compile error. Lifecycle
LIF-228 Restore bytes MUST be passed to the new build only when its data_version equals the one of the build that produced them. Otherwise they are dropped and the host logs restore.dropped-data-version. change data_version between two builds. Lifecycle
LIF-229 The dev instance MUST be held by a lease. The ilium plugin dev process renews it every 2 s over its connection. The server MUST remove the dev package and restore the installed version when the lease is not renewed for 10 s, or when the connection closes. kill the dev process with SIGKILL and assert the installed version returns within 10 s. Lifecycle
LIF-270 A stop after three breaches MUST end at an instance restart of the contributor or Reset and MUST NOT be persisted. stop an extension, restart the contributor, and call it. extension points
LIF-271 On a trap or stop the host MUST release every effect listed in the stop-effects paragraph of this page, for the dead instance as well. trap a plugin holding an input lock, a stream and a child process. Lifecycle
LIF-272 Enable from the recovery page MUST clear the failure window, and Reset failures MUST clear it without activating. fail a plugin three times, press each. Building settings screens
LIF-273 A replacement disabled by failure MUST re-enable the replaced core plugin with a visible notice. the replacement is disabled by the restart and disable rule (three crashes). Extending core plugins
LIF-274 The host MUST activate inactive contributors of an active owner in the background. owner activates, contributor is active without a call. extension points
LIF-275 An update MUST reset the "Not now" counter of a bundled plugin. answer Not now twice, update, and count prompts. Lifecycle
LIF-276 The Plugins screen MUST not offer a disable switch for the four essential plugins. render the list and press Space on each. Core plugins
LIF-277 data_version MUST be an integer from 0 to 4,294,967,295, and a stored version above the manifest value MUST follow the downgrade rule of the migration guide. -1 is refused with manifest.schema; a stored 3 with manifest 2 is handled as a downgrade. Manifest reference
LIF-278 A manifest with data_version above 1 MUST list migrator in exports for each of its server and client components, and each of those components MUST export it. Checked at stage 6 with manifest.exports-mismatch. omit it from one component and expect manifest.exports-mismatch. Manifest reference
LIF-279 The fake host MUST offer the methods in the table, and its results MUST match the real host for the lines above. run the same fixtures against both. Testing plugins
LIF-280 A provider failure MUST NOT count as a failure of its consumers. trap a provider and read the consumer window. Services
LIF-281 Uninstall MUST remove the plugin grants, and a project folder MUST NOT be able to install or enable a plugin. uninstall and read grants.json; list an uninstalled package in plugins.toml. Security model
LIF-282 The host MUST validate installed.json against the schema above at start and refuse a file that does not match it with install.state-corrupt, without rewriting it. write one file per property with a wrong type, an extra key, a short key_id and a local-time installed_at, and assert install.state-corrupt for each. Install, update and uninstall
LIF-283 The package states disabled-untrusted and disabled-blocked MUST follow rows P13 to P16, MUST be stored in installed.json and MUST survive a restart. A plugin in either state MUST NOT run, and MUST keep its grants, settings and data. remove the signing key with --force, restart the server and assert disabled-untrusted; revoke a key as compromised and assert disabled-blocked; leave each state by the stated way. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-284 A side whose required plugin or service provider is not active MUST be in the instance state waiting-dependency, MUST NOT count a failure, and MUST follow rows I16 to I18. activate a consumer while its provider is disabled, assert waiting-dependency, enable the provider and assert activating; repeat with a provider that stays off for longer than wait_ms and assert inactive with dependency.unresolved. Reference, plugin lifecycle states
LIF-285 The failure window is per plugin, per side, per scope and per version. It MUST be emptied when the active version changes, on ilium plugin dev reload and on a manual enable. The first activation failure of an update candidate is not counted (LIF-075), and a manual ilium plugin restart <id> neither counts nor empties the window. trap twice, change the active version and trap again and assert 1 failure; repeat for dev reload and enable; fail a candidate's first activation and assert the window is empty; restart manually and assert the count is unchanged. Lifecycle
